title: Interest is charged only on Utilized USDS, so idle borrowed liquidity costs a Prime nothing
content:
A.2.4.2.1.2 defines the interest base as "utilized USDS," being liquidity a Prime borrowed from Sky less five deductions: USDS held idle in an ALM Proxy, idle in a Peg Stability Module, attributable to a Sky Direct Exposure, idle in an AMM pool, and "supplied to a lending pool that is not borrowed from that pool."

The principle is that Sky charges for capital *put to work*, not for capital drawn. Each deduction identifies a state where borrowed USDS exists but is not generating a return for the Prime — including the subtle final case, where supplying a lending pool only earns once someone borrows against it.

The incentives this creates are the right ones. A Prime can hold operational buffers, keep liquidity staged for an opportunity, or leave depth in an AMM without paying a carry on it, so prudent liquidity management is free rather than penalised. It also removes any reason to route funds back and forth to avoid an interest meter, which would burn gas and add execution risk for no economic purpose.

The corresponding cost falls on measurement. "Idle" is a state that must be observed continuously across several venue types on multiple chains, and each deduction is a place where a Prime's reported figure and Sky's could legitimately differ — which is precisely the kind of line item the five-day dispute window in the settlement process exists to contest.

Excluding Sky Direct Exposures fits the same logic from the other direction: where Sky itself holds the exposure, the Prime is not the party using the liquidity and should not be charged for it.
description: Balances sitting in an ALM Proxy, a PSM, an AMM pool, unborrowed lending-pool supply, and Sky Direct Exposures are all deducted before interest accrues on borrowed liquidity.
